text: Spin-coated CsPb(I1-xBrx)3 films with x from 0 to 1 show band gaps ranging from 1.73 to 2.31 eV. The x = 0.5 film has a Tauc gap of 1.95 eV.
Cu2O films electrodeposited at different pH values have band gaps between 2.0 and 2.4 eV as measured by UV-vis spectroscopy. We use the film grown at pH 11 (gap 2.12 eV) for device fabrication.
Reported band gap values for ZnO range from 3.1 to 3.4 eV depending on the preparation route. Our own nanoparticles show no distinct absorption edge, so no gap could be extracted.

UV-vis transmission shows that the sapphire substrate is transparent down to 200 nm, i.e. its band gap exceeds 6.2 eV and it does not absorb the excitation. The Ga2O3 film on top has an optical gap of 4.9 eV.
The conductivity of the GeSn alloy increases with temperature, indicating a narrow band gap below 0.5 eV. The sheet resistance at room temperature is 120 ohm per square.
PBE calculations show that all five candidate halides have gaps larger than 3 eV, while for CsSnBr3 specifically we obtain a gap of 0.8 eV.
Applying 5% biaxial strain reduces the PBE band gap of monolayer MoS2 from 1.68 eV to 1.35 eV, i.e. by 0.33 eV.
Compared with pristine g-C3N4 (2.74 eV by diffuse reflectance), the S-doped sample shows a red shift of the absorption edge corresponding to a band gap narrowing of 0.21 eV.
The optical band gap of the Si-doped Ga2O3 film shrinks by 0.15 eV relative to the undoped film, whose Tauc gap is 4.85 eV.
The gap of the PbSe quantum dots is roughly 0.9 eV, corresponding to a first exciton absorption peak at about 1380 nm.
UV-vis absorption indicates that the band gap of the Zn2SnO4 film is ~3.6 eV.
In the TiO2/g-C3N4 heterojunction the Tauc plot gives an effective band gap of 2.95 eV, lying between the 3.20 eV of pure TiO2 and the 2.70 eV of pure g-C3N4 measured under identical conditions.

The type-II band alignment between WS2 and MoS2 is characterized by a valence band offset of 0.55 eV and a conduction band offset of 0.35 eV from XPS. The WS2/MoS2 heterobilayer shows an interlayer optical gap of 1.35 eV in photoluminescence.
Band offsets at the GaN/AlN interface measured by XPS are 0.7 eV for the conduction band and 1.0 eV for the valence band, so the two materials differ in gap by 1.7 eV.

Table 1 lists the Tauc gaps of three CdSxSe1-x films: CdSe 1.74 eV, CdS0.5Se0.5 2.05 eV and CdS 2.40 eV. The PBE calculations in Section 3 underestimate all three, giving 0.45, 0.95 and 1.12 eV, respectively.
The gap of our SnO2 film, 3.60 eV by diffuse reflectance, is in good agreement with the 3.55 eV found by Zhang et al. and the 3.65 eV found by Lee et al.
The spectrometer was calibrated on a reference TiO2 P25 sample, for which a Tauc gap of 3.20 eV was obtained, before measuring the BiOCl nanosheets, which gave 3.35 eV.
SnS2 films were illuminated with a 405 nm laser. Their absorption edge, taken as the optical band gap, lies at 540 nm.

text: For wurtzite CdS we obtain a band gap of 1.15 eV with PBE, 2.35 eV with HSE06 and 2.75 eV with GW; the experimental value of 2.42 eV is taken from Ref. 23.
For single-layer WSe2 on graphite, STS gives a gap of 2.20 eV, while the photoluminescence optical gap of the same sample is 1.65 eV. The 0.55 eV difference reflects the exciton binding energy.

text: From photoluminescence excitation spectra, the band gap of In0.53Ga0.47As is 0.75 eV at 300 K and 0.81 eV at 77 K.
The CdSe/ZnS core-shell quantum dots emit at 620 nm with a quantum yield of 85% and a full width at half maximum of 28 nm.
The OQMD database lists a gap of 1.6 eV for Cs2SnI6, whereas our HSE06 calculation gives 1.2 eV.
Co-doped TiO2 nanoparticles (3 at% Co) show a Tauc gap of 2.78 eV, compared with 3.10 eV for the undoped nanoparticles.
The Tran-Blaha modified Becke-Johnson potential gives a gap of 3.2 eV for cubic SrTiO3, while scanning tunneling spectroscopy on our SrTiO3 film measures 3.3 eV.
Diffuse reflectance spectra indicate band gaps of about 3.4, 2.8 and 1.8 eV for the BiOCl, BiOBr and BiOI nanoplates, respectively.
InAs0.91Sb0.09 epilayers on GaSb show a cut-off wavelength of 4.5 µm at 300 K, which corresponds to the band gap of the alloy.
The silicon photonic crystal has a photonic band gap centered at 1550 nm with a width of 120 nm. The electronic band gap of silicon (1.12 eV) is well known.
Mott-Schottky analysis of the BiVO4 photoanode gives a flat-band potential of 0.1 V vs RHE and a carrier density of 3e19 cm-3. The optical band gap of the same film is 2.5 eV.

gold.evidence: optical band gap of the same film is 2.5 eV
